teaser: A ledger gets checked twice before anyone signs it, not because the first count was wrong. Life path 7 and ESTJ sit together in you as a seeker who wants hard proof and a supervisor who wants it filed correctly. In a hotel lobby, waiting for a delayed checkout to clear, you read the whole situation before the desk clerk finishes a sentence — not suspicion, just the habit of wanting the real answer before the official one. The 7 wants the truth underneath; the ESTJ wants the truth on record. In you those are close to the same thing, and that is rarer than it sounds.
excerpt: A paper cup of vending-machine coffee goes cold between two people in a hospital cafeteria, waiting on news from someone else's room.
